meta.title: MHXX quest resource formats (.arc and inner resources)

confidence_levels.confirmed: 実データ/逆コンパイル済みソースで直接確認

fields.encoding: Shift_JIS (Quest_Construct writes Shift-JIS; sample names are ASCII)
fields.note: NUL terminated, rest zero-filled; folder separators are BACKSLASH; extension is NOT stored
= 0x40000000 | uncompressed_size ; uncompressed_size is effectively 24-bit; the tool writes 3 bytes then a literal 0x40
absolute offset from the beginning of the .arc

data_region.compression: zlib RFC1950 stream (first two bytes observed: 78 01 x189, 78 9C x1761)
data_region.layout: entries are stored back to back with no gaps; file size == last_entry.data_offset + last_entry.compressed_size (141/141)
data_region.entry_order: grouped by folder in a fixed order (boss, zako, rem, supp, plus, questLink, questData*_jpn, questData); within a folder the order can differ from the .qdl order
data_region.padding: the gap between the entry table and the first data byte is all zero (141/141)

type_hashes.source: Quest_Construct.decompiled.cs lines 94-109 and 102-109 (file_ei[]) - exact integer literals match the .arc values
type_hashes.formula_search: NOT IDENTIFIED. Brute-forced 466 candidate strings x 17 hash functions (CRC32/CRC32C/CRC32-BZIP2/CRC32K, FNV-1, FNV-1a, DJB2 both variants, SDBM, Jenkins one-at-a-time, h*31+c, h*33+c, h*0x21+c, h*0x21^c, h*0x25+c, MurmurHash3 x86_32 (seed 0/1), xxHash32, Adler32) over extension/type-name variants: no match. Treat the table as a constant lookup.
type_hashes.note: the same 32-bit value also appears inside payloads (questLink .qdl records, .mib offset 223) as a sibling resource-type reference

read_procedure: read u16 version (expect 17) and u16 entry_count
for i in 0..entry_count: read the 80-byte entry
write_procedure: 1. collect the files to pack (folder layout quest/<folder>/<name>.<ext>)
2. zlib-compress each payload (DotNetZip ZlibStream, CompressionLevel.Default => header 78 9C); the game accepts 78 01 too
3. entry_count = number of files; data_start = 12 + 80*entry_count + 20 (Quest_Construct) or align32(12 + 80*entry_count) to reproduce Capcom layout
4. write magic 0x00435241 (little endian 41 52 43 00), u16 17, u16 entry_count, u32 0

5. for each entry: name = 'quest\\' + folder + '\\' + basename_without_ext (Shift_JIS, max 64 bytes, zero padded); type_hash from the table; compressed_size = len(zlib); flags = 0x40000000 | uncompressed_size (write 3 bytes of size then the byte 0x40); data_offset
6. write payloads back to back starting at data_start
reproducibility: decompress(repack(extract(arc))) == original payloads for all 1950 entries of the 141 sample arcs
sanity_rules: supp / plus / questLink / questData(.mib) / questData(.gmd) always exist (1 each per quest)
boss/setEmMain and zako/emSetList carry a mandatory dummy payload (b_m00em000_00, z_m00d_000) so their counts are >= 1

the physical entry set equals the set of unique names referenced by the 15 .qdl records plus questLink_<id>, questData_<id>_jpn, questData_<id> (139/141 exact including order; 2 files differ only in order or in the embedded id - see notes)
q1011045.arc contains resources named *_1011043 while its .mib says 1011045: never synthesise names from the file name, always read them from the entries

unknown_region_88_99.note: bytes 84..87 (rem1..rem3) are included in the printed 16-byte window; the 12 unknown bytes are 88..99. 88/89 and 94/95 tend to hold equal values - possibly u16 pairs. Quedixx never reads or writes them.

gmd.description: UTF-8 text table for one quest (7 strings). Capcom/MT Framework GMD.

fields.note: 0x432F44B3 in 139/141; 0x44AAB360 (q1010172) and 0x44A0B4EC (q1011028) otherwise. Not equal to any common hash of the resource name; treat as opaque and preserve.
= file_size - 58 = total bytes of the 7 NUL-terminated strings
length of the resource name without the NUL

string_table.encoding: UTF-8, NUL terminated, CRLF line breaks inside
string_table.label_evidence: tabPage2 labels: label3 クエスト名 / label18 依頼内容 / label17 依頼主 / label16 主なモンスター / label15 サブ成功条件 / label14 失敗条件 / label13 成功条件; txt_read maps strings[0..6] to textBox1..7
string_table.note: string blob size == sum(len)+7 exactly (141/141); only Japanese (_jpn) gmd files are shipped in this sample set - no multi-language variant was found

gmd.rewrite_rule: Quedixx txt_edit: new_size = 58 + sum(utf8_len(s)+1); copy the first 58 bytes of the old file, write the new blob size at offset 32, then append the 7 strings. (If the resource name length ever differs from 17 the fixed 58 must be replaced by 40+name_length+1.)

qdl.evidence: 141/141 files have exactly 15 records and no remainder
qdl.note: A .qdl slot may repeat the same name (dummy slot); the physical .arc contains each unique name only once. The .qdl never references questData/questLink itself.
qdl.editor_rule: Quedixx link_edit overwrites 15x16 bytes at 20*i+12; it cannot grow or shrink the file. link_read reads the same window. If an .arc legitimately needs more than 15 references this format cannot express it.

sem.note: Quedixx oomons_edit preserves the file size; the 4 extra bytes beyond the fields it edits are copied verbatim.
sem.ui_mapping_evidence: tabPage6 Location pairing: label46 エリア->o_o0(+12), label50 向き->o_o1(+16), label54 X->o_o2(+20), label52 Z->o_o3(+24), label51 Y->o_o4(+28)

fields.note: absolute file offsets of up to 14 ESD chunks. 0 = slot empty. Chunk i ends at the next non-zero offset, or EOF. Only indices 0..10 were observed in use; 11..13 were always 0.

chunk.evidence: 674/674 chunks across 141 files satisfy the rule

record.note: the three f32 at +12/+16/+20 look like a position; +28 looks like a monster id (e.g. 0x6B30 = 27440). Not exposed by Quedixx (komons_read/komons_edit are no-ops).

esl.empty_form: a 64-byte header with every chunk offset 0 (60 of 141 zako resources are exactly this)

fields.note: Quedixx exposes it as 8 rows x 2 columns and round-trips it. Values observed: col0 in 1..8, col1 in 1..0x16; the all-zero resource rem_000000 is all zeros here as well.

rem.note: rem_000000 is a byte-identical all-zero dummy in all 101 files that contain it - use it as the empty slot.

sup.note: Quedixx sikyu_read uses num=8 for .sup (records start right after the 8-byte header) and num=24 for .rem (records start after the 8-byte header + the 16-byte table).

qdp.note: Quedixx plus_read/plus_edit are no-ops (the payload is preserved byte for byte). The values 1/20/40/90/600 and the constant low u16 = 1 suggest u16 pairs, but the exact field boundaries are undetermined.

quest_id.format: 7 decimal digits, d1 d2 d3 d4 d5 d6 d7
quest_id.id_range_check: Quedixx oq_id NumericUpDown: Minimum 101, Maximum 1120050, default 1000001
quest_id.note: the id lives in .mib offset 12 and in the resource names (questData_<id>, supp_<id>, questLink_<id>). new_quest.exe rewrites all of them and renames the file: main_file_edit replaces the old id string inside the file name.
